## Évolution & Biologie

## Ce qu'il faut retenir

L'œil est le résultat de **~450 millions d'années** d'évolution, depuis les simples cellules photosensibles jusqu'à l'œil vertébré complexe.

Les **6 étapes clés** de l'évolution de l'œil :

1. Cellules photosensibles planes (pas de directionnalité)
2. Zone déprimée → sensibilité directionnelle limitée
3. Œil à sténopé (*pinhole*) → imagerie rudimentaire
4. Chambre close avec humeur transparente → rétine distincte
5. Apparition d'un cristallin → focalisation
6. Iris + cornée séparée → œil moderne complet

## Historical Theories of Vision

## The main stages

| Epoch | Author | Key idea | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~350 BC AD | Plato | Light *emitted* by the eyes | ❌ False |
| ~330 BC AD | Aristotle | Material images entering the eye | ❌ Incomplete |
| ~1040 | **Alhazen** | Light traveling towards the eye, pointillism | ✅ Founder |
| ~1600 | **Kepler** | Retinal theory, separation by refraction | ✅ Correct |
| Modern | — | Psychology + neurophysiology + computational vision | ✅ |

## Alhazen — key takeaways

- Light travels **in a straight line**
- Self-luminous body → irradiation in **all directions**
- Vision = collection of **points** on the surfaces of objects
- **Geometric correspondence** world ↔ retinal image

## Kepler — key takeaway

> Rays from the same surface point arrive at the lens from **different directions** → refracted differently → **focused at a single point** on the retina.

## Characteristics of HVS

## Essential numbers to memorize

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Visual acuity (20/20) | $\approx 1$ arc minute |
| Horizontal field | $\approx 200°$ ($120°$ binocular + $2 \times 40°$ monocular) |
| Vertical field | $\approx 135°$ |
| Temporal resolution | $\approx 60$ Hz |
| Instantaneous dynamic range | $6{,}5$ stops |
| Adapted dynamic range | $46{,}5$ stops ($\approx 14$ orders of magnitude) |
| Accommodation (young) | $\approx 8$ cm → $\infty$ |
| Accommodation (50 years) | $\approx 50$ cm → $\infty$ |
| Sticks | $\approx 10^8$ |
| Cones | $\approx 10^7$ |
| Optic nerve fibers | $\approx 10^6$ |

⚠️ The ratio of $10^8$ photoreceptors / $10^6$ nerve fibers imposes mandatory **coding/compression** of the visual signal.

## Eye Anatomy

## Structure from front to back

```{.mermaid}
graph LR
    A[Cornée\n~2/3 puissance dioptrique] --> B[Humeur aqueuse]
    B --> C[Iris + Pupille\nØ 2–8 mm]
    C --> D[Cristallin\naccommodation]
    D --> E[Humeur vitrée]
    E --> F[Rétine\nphotorécepteurs]
    F --> G[Nerf optique]
```

**Critical points:**

- **Cornea**: main refractive surface
- **Pupil**: controls the amount of light (like the aperture of a camera)
- **Fovea**: high resolution area, rich in cones
- **Blind spot** (optic disc): no photoreceptor → blind spot in the visual field

## Retina & Photoreceptors

## Two parallel systems

| | **Rods** | **Cones (Cones)** |
|---|---|---|
| Vision | Scotopic (low light) | Photopic (good light) |
| Resolution | **Low** | **High** |
| Sensitivity | **High** | Bass |
| Color | No (grayscale) | **Yes** (S, M, L) |
| Convergence | Strong (↓ resolution) | Low (↑ resolution) |
| Location | Periphery | Fovea |

## The 3 types of cones

1. **S** (*Short*) → $\approx 419$ nm → **blue** (weak response)
2. **M** (*Medium*) → $\approx 531$ nm → **green** (dominant response)
3. **L** (*Long*) → $\approx 559$ nm → **red** (near infrared)

## Limitations of the human eye

- Blood vessels **in front** of photoreceptors (inverted eye)
- Image **reversed** on the retina
- **High resolution only in the fovea**
- **Blind spot** at the optic disc
- Non-uniform brightness on the retina

---

## Retinal Ganglion Cells

## Fundamental role

> Replace **absolute levels** of brightness with a map of **differences** (retinotopic map).

## Center-surround organization

- **ON-center / OFF-surround**: activated by light in the center, inhibited at the periphery
- **OFF-center / ON-surround**: reverse

**Why?** Objects are identified by their *differences* with the background, not by their absolute brightness → allows amplification without saturation.

## M vs P cells

| | **M (Magnocellular)** | **P (Parvocellular)** |
|---|---|---|
| Size | Large | Small |
| Speed ​​| Fast | Nits |
| Spatial resolution | Bass | **High** |
| Temporal resolution | **High** | Bass |
| Color | No | **Yes** |
| Role | Movement, sudden stimuli | Color, texture, shapes |
| LGN power supply | Magnocellular layers | Parvocellular layers |

---

## Visual Pathways & Cortex

## Complete processing chain

```{.mermaid}
graph TD
    R[Rétine\nPhotorécepteurs → Ganglionnaires] --> OC[Chiasma optique\nDécussation fibres nasales]
    OC --> LGN[LGN\n2 couches M + 4 couches P]
    LGN --> V1[V1 Cortex visuel primaire\nCellules simples + complexes]
    V1 --> D[Flux DORSAL\nWHERE — Mouvement, localisation]
    V1 --> V[Flux VENTRAL\nWHAT — Reconnaissance objets]
    D --> CP[Cortex pariétal]
    V --> CT[Cortex temporal\nFFA, PPA...]
```

## LGN — to remember

- **1 LGN per hemisphere**
- **6 layers**: 2 magnocellular (M) + 4 parvocellular (P)
- **Retinotopia preserved** in all layers
- All neurons: organization **center-surround**

## V1 — 3 types of cells (Hubel & Wiesel, Nobel Prize)

1. **Center-surround**: identical to LGN

2. **Simple cells**:
   - Elongated receptive fields (excitatory + inhibitory)
   - Respond to **contours with precise orientation and position**
   - Constructed from several aligned center-surround fields

3. **Complex cells**:
   - More abstract, **partially position invariant**
   - Respond to oriented contours over a *range* of positions

## Feedforward hierarchy

$$\text{Centre-entourage} \rightarrow \text{Simple} \rightarrow \text{Complexe}$$

- Increasing specificity to **form**
- Increasing generality to **observation conditions**
- ⇒ Basis of **object recognition**

## Hypercolumns in V1

Spatial organization minimizing the distance between neurons for similar stimuli according to:

- **Original eye** (left / right)
- **Preferred orientation**
- **Retinotopic localization**

> *Hebb’s rule: “Neurons that fire together, wire together.” »*

## Contrast Sensitivity Function (CSF)

- Peak sensitivity: $\approx 4$–$6$ cycles per degree (cpd)
- Upper limit: $\approx 60$ cpd (cone packing density)
- The curve **moves** with the observation distance

## Ventral flow — progression

| Level | Receptive field | Latency | Specialty |
|---|---|---|---|
| NGL | $1°$ | — | Center-surround |
| V1 | $1°$ | 40–60ms | Guidance |
| V2 | $1{,}3°$ | 50–70ms | — |
| V4 | $4{,}8°$ | 60–80ms | Color, shapes |
| TEO | $5{,}8°$ | 70–90ms | Feature combinations |
| TE | $12°$ | 80–100ms | Independence of view |

## Link with Computational Vision

## Biological inspirations → algorithms

| Biology | Algorithm / Model |
|---|---|
| Orientation selectivity V1 | **SIFT**, **HOG** |
| Single cells (oriented filters) | **Convolution** layers |
| Complex cells (local invariance) | **pooling** layers |
| Ventral flow hierarchy | **Neocognitron** → **CNN** |

## Neocognitron (Fukushima, 1980)

$$U_0 \rightarrow U_{S1} \rightarrow U_{C1} \rightarrow U_{S2} \rightarrow U_{C2} \rightarrow U_{S3} \rightarrow U_{C3}$$

- $U_S$ layers (simple type): synapses **modifiable**
- $U_C$ layers (complex type): **fixed** synapses, position invariance

## LeNet (LeCun et al., 1998)

$$\text{Image} \rightarrow \text{Conv} \rightarrow \text{Pool} \rightarrow \text{Conv} \rightarrow \text{Pool} \rightarrow \text{Dense} \rightarrow \text{Sortie}$$

## Applications — 3D & VR displays

## Principle of stereoscopy

Two slightly offset images (binocular disparity) → each eye receives its image → the brain perceives **depth**.

## Vergence-Accommodation Conflict (VAC)

⚠️ **Central problem with stereoscopic displays**:

| | Real world | Classic stereo display |
|---|---|---|
| **Vergence** | Object distance | Virtual distance (disparity) |
| **Accommodation** | Object distance | Physical distance from screen (fixed) |
| **Pairing** | ✅ Always coupled | ❌ Decoupled → **conflict** |

**Effects of VAC:**

- Visual discomfort, fatigue, nausea
- Split vision (*diplopic vision*)
- Degradation of perceived image quality
- Risk of pathologies (visual systems in development)

## ACV solutions

- **Gaze-contingent Focus Displays**: eye tracking + mechanical movement of the focal plane
- **Near-eye Light Field Displays**: simulation of several focal planes simultaneously
- **Holographic displays**: complete wavefront reconstruction → natural accommodation

## Comfort zone

The greater the **observation distance**, the wider the comfort zone:

$$\text{Mobile} < \text{Desktop} < \text{TV} < \text{Cinéma}$$

---

## Absolute Key Points to Remember

- **Rods** → sensitivity, movement, night — **Cones** → resolution, color, day
- **M Cells** → temporal (movement) — **P Cells** → spatial (color, shape)
- **Dorsal flow** → *Where* — **Ventral flow** → *What*
- **V1**: simple cells (precise orientation) → complex (partial invariance)
- **CSF** peak: $4$–$6$ cpd
- **VAC** = fundamental problem with 3D displays
- **CNN** = computational implementation of the ventral flow hierarchy
